headline: stdio vs Streamable HTTP: Picking an MCP Transport
description: A threshold-based comparison of the two MCP transports: what each looks like at the byte level, what the 2026-07-28 stateless revision changed about the tradeoff, which capabilities exist on only one side, and how to support both.
keywords: MCP stdio vs HTTP, MCP transport, Streamable HTTP, stdio transport, Model Context Protocol transport, MCP transport comparison, Mcp-Method header, Mcp-Param, x-mcp-header, MRTR, 2026-07-28, stateless MCP, HTTP+SSE deprecated, custom MCP transport

about.name: MCP stdio transport
about.description: Transport binding where the client launches the server as a subprocess and exchanges newline-delimited JSON-RPC messages over standard streams

about.name: MCP Streamable HTTP transport
about.description: Transport binding where each JSON-RPC message is an HTTP POST to a single MCP endpoint, answered with a JSON object or a request-scoped SSE stream

about.name: Transport binding
about.description: In MCP, a definition of message framing, delivery, request metadata carriage, and cancellation signaling; protocol semantics are identical across bindings

about.name: Standard request headers
about.description: MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, and Mcp-Name headers mirrored from the body on Streamable HTTP so intermediaries can route without parsing it

about.name: x-mcp-header
about.description: Tool schema annotation that mirrors a primitive tool argument into an Mcp-Param-{Name} HTTP header for gateway-level routing

about.name: Multi Round-Trip Requests
about.description: The pattern replacing server-initiated JSON-RPC requests: a server returns an InputRequiredResult and the client retries the original call with responses

about.name: HTTP+SSE transport
about.description: The 2024-11-05 transport with separate SSE and POST endpoints, deprecated since 2025-03-26 and eligible for removal under the feature lifecycle policy

about.name: Custom MCP transports
about.description: Non-standard bindings that must preserve JSON-RPC format, message patterns, and per-request metadata; byte-stream channels should reuse stdio framing

mainEntity.name: Which MCP transport should I use for a local developer tool?

acceptedAnswer.text: stdio. The host spawns your server as a child process, it inherits the user's environment and privileges, and you get per-user isolation for free with no network surface, no TLS, and no authorization layer to design.

mainEntity.name: Can one MCP server support both stdio and Streamable HTTP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is normal. Protocol semantics are identical across transports, so you register tools, resources, and prompts once and wire two entry points around them: serveStdio(factory) and createMcpHandler(factory) in the TypeScript SDK. The only things that do not transfer are local machine access and anything built assuming session state.

mainEntity.name: Is Streamable HTTP still hard to scale horizontally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not the way it was. The 2026-07-28 revision removed the Mcp-Session-Id header and the protocol-level session, so any request can land on any instance and a plain round-robin load balancer is sufficient. The sticky sessions and shared session store that horizontal deployments needed under 2025-11-25 are no longer required at the protocol layer.

mainEntity.name: Why does my stdio MCP server disconnect with JSON parse errors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Something is writing to stdout that is not an MCP message. On stdio, stdout is the JSON-RPC channel and messages are newline-delimited with no embedded newlines permitted, so a single console.log from your code or a dependency corrupts the stream. Log to stderr instead: the specification explicitly permits it and clients should not treat stderr output as an error signal.

mainEntity.name: What happened to SSE as an MCP transport?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two different things get called SSE. The 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE transport with separate SSE and POST endpoints is deprecated and eligible for removal. Separately, Streamable HTTP still uses SSE, but as a response format scoped to a single request rather than a long-lived channel for server-initiated messages. The standalone GET stream was removed in 2026-07-28.

mainEntity.name: Can I use WebSocket or gRPC with MCP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not as a standard transport, and the 2026 roadmap states no new official transports this cycle. You may implement a custom transport provided you preserve the JSON-RPC message format, the message patterns, and the per-request metadata model. If your channel is a reliable bidirectional byte stream such as a Unix domain socket or TCP, the specification recommends reusing the stdio framing, which existing implementations already speak.

mainEntity.name: How do I keep state between MCP tool calls if there is no session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mint an explicit handle from a tool and have the model pass it back as an ordinary argument on later calls. It works identically on both transports, it survives an instance dying or a stdio process restarting, and it stays visible during debugging rather than hidden in transport metadata.
